A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DoL is a consequence of spatial patterning of agents, and the latter is a consequence of the stochastic nature of the environment.
division of labour in insect societies is an emergent property of the system that is driven by the spatial patterning of individual workers.
the division of labour in biological systems is not a result of the variation in response thresholds of individuals, but rather a result of the spatial distribution of individuals.
The main takeaway from our work is that

spatial patterning and non-random distributions of individuals in social systems are a natural consequence of the principle of Do L, and not a consequence of the direct interactions between the individuals themselves.
the division of labour can emerge even in the absence of any agent-agent interaction, but rather by the indirect interactions between individuals mediated by the environment.
the spatial patterning of the individuals is the key to understanding division of labour.
